newsitem.title: HONG KONG: China's Jiangling profit soars on lower costs.
newsitem.headline: China's Jiangling profit soars on lower costs.

text.p: Jiangling Motors Corp Ltd on Wednesday attributed its huge 1996 profit rise to success in capping production costs with help from shareholder Ford Motor Co.
Jiangling said net profit for 1996 rose 776 percent to 34.62 million yuan from 3.95 million yuan a year earlier, based on international accounting standards.

Ford, which currently holds a 20 percent stake in Jiangling, helped improve cost controls and streamline management, a Jiangling spokesman told the Hong Kong-based newsletter China Securities Bulletin.

"Profit margins widened as Jiangling used more China-made car parts, which are cheaper," the spokesman said, adding that the domestic content of its vehicles rose to 80 percent in 1996 from 60 percent in 1995.
But a fall in sale prices caused by sharp competition limited the Chinese light truck maker's gains, he said.
Turnover was 1.69 billion yuan against 1.97 billion yuan in 1995 under Chinese standards, according to the company.
Jiangling would begin making light commercial vehicles with Ford's help in the second half of 1997, the spokesman said.
The project, which will cost between 500 million and 700 million yuan, was likely to become Jianlging's second major profit source when it begins full operations in 1998, he said.
Jiangling will issue 170 million new B shares in June to help raise funds for the light-vehicle project.
Ford in 1995 paid about US$40 million to buy 80 percent of Jiangling's 174 million B shares. The U.S. firm will also buy 120 million shares of the new issue for $54.5 million.
After the offer, Ford would hold close to 30 percent of Jiangling's outstanding shares, Jiangling said.
Jiangling said it had appointed Shenzhen J&A Securities as the domestic lead underwriter, but declined to name the international coordinator.
